US-10041219.summary: The patent describes a reusable hand scraper system for waste removal, comprising a bag and a pair of scrapers. Each scraper has a panel with surfaces and a peripheral edge, a strap for securing the scraper to the hand, and a hazard detection unit. The bag is positioned over animal waste, and the scrapers are used to push the waste into the bag, which is then closed with a closure. The system includes various sensors for detecting hazards and a strap mechanism to secure the scrapers to the hands.
US-10041219.mechanism: The system uses a bag and a pair of scrapers to urge animal waste into the bag. The scrapers are manipulated by the user to push the waste into the bag, which is then closed using a closure.
key_claim_elements: A hand scraper system for waste removal comprising a bag and a pair of scrapers.

Each scraper has a panel with a first surface, a second surface, and a peripheral edge, with the upper side of the peripheral edge configured to have a user's hand positioned thereon and the lower side configured to urge animal waste into the bag.

Each scraper also has a strap coupled to the first surface, separated from the upper side toward the lower side, and wrapping around the panel to extend along the second surface, configured to be wrapped around the hand.
The panel comprises a plurality of finger indentations traversing into the second surface.
The bag is configured to be positioned over animal waste, with a closure coupled to the bag to retain the waste inside.
The bag comprises a bottom wall and a peripheral wall extending upwardly from the bottom wall, with the peripheral wall having an outer surface and a distal edge defining an opening into the bag.
The closure is positioned on the outer surface and is substantially coextensive with the distal edge, with a pair of ends configured to be tied together to close the opening.
The hazard detection unit is positioned proximate the lower side of the panel and can be removably attached to the panel.
The strap comprises a first end and a second end, each being matable, and is configured to retain the panel on the hand.
The strap may include a first coupler and a second coupler, which are complementary and configured to retain the panel on the hand.
implementation_unknowns: The exact type of hazard detection unit is not specified, as it can be a toxic gas sensor, chemical vapor sensor, explosives detection sensor, radiation sensor, or bio sensor.

US-10052665.summary: The patent describes a cleaning device designed to dispense fluid onto a surface and then wipe it off. The device includes a housing with an outer and inner portion, a dispenser with a porous material for delivering fluid, and a wiper with a stiff inner core and an outer fabric layer. The wiper can be repositioned to use different parts of the fabric. The device can also include caps for the dispenser and wiper. The dispenser and wiper have specific dimensions for their protruding portions. Another embodiment describes a housing with separate cavities for the dispenser and wiper, with the wiper core being slightly smaller than its cavity to allow for easy positioning.
US-10052665.mechanism: The cleaning device works by having a dispenser that selectively delivers fluid to a surface being cleaned and a wiper that wipes the dispensed fluid from the surface. The wiper can be repositioned to use different portions of the outer fabric layer.

A cleaning device configured to selectively dispense a fluid to a surface being cleaned, the cleaning device comprising: a housing comprising a first end and a second end, the first end comprising a dispenser cavity and the second end comprising a wiper cavity; a dispenser positioned at least partially within the dispenser cavity, the dispenser comprising a porous or fluid permeable material; wherein the dispenser comprises a dispensing portion at least partially protruding from the dispenser cavity, the dispensing portion configured to contact a surface being cleaned and to selectively deliver fluid thereto; and a wiper removably positioned at least partially within the wiper cavity, the wiper comprising a wiper core wrapped in at least one layer of fabric; wherein the wiper core and the wiper cavity each comprise a thickness, and the thickness of the wiper cavity is greater than the thickness of the wiper core.

US-10052751.mechanism: The device uses a braking cylinder with a brake shoe and a locking handle. The handle has a pusher that applies force to the brake shoe to retain the pole section.

US-10064481.summary: The claims describe a textile-machine cleaning brush element that is fastened to a cylindrical base body. Claim 1 defines a skeleton of concentric support rings and longitudinal webs, a spiked lattice over the skeleton, and a rubber sealing compound connecting them, with a cylindrical hollow element formed by a tube component or rubber inner surface. Dependent claims add interlocking ends, coupling pieces, recessed or raised inner surfaces, plug-in skeleton components, a polyamide skeleton, and U-shaped wire hooks. An independent claim describes a brush comprising a shaft and the cleaning element. The claims do not specify a motor, battery, heater, electric pump, or other power source, so powered status is unclear.
US-10064481.mechanism: A modular brush element is assembled over a cylindrical base body using a ring-and-web skeleton, spiked lattice, and rubber sealing compound; adjacent elements can be rotationally locked by interlocking ends or a coupling piece to form a continuous cleaning brush.

US-10065611.summary: The patent describes a windshield cleaning implement with an arcuate, flexible shaft and a cleaning head that can simultaneously hold a sponge, a scrubbing brush, and a wiper blade. These elements are removably attached to the cleaning head via tubular slots, allowing the user to dampen, scrub, and scrape a windshield in one motion. The device is operated manually via a handle at the proximal end of the shaft.
US-10065611.mechanism: The windshield cleaning implement has an arcuate, flexible shaft with a cleaning head at its distal end. The cleaning head features multiple tubular slots on its front face, allowing for the removable attachment of a sponge, a wiper blade, and a scrubbing brush. The sponge, scrubbing brush, and wiper blade can be simultaneously used to dampen, scrub, and scrape a windshield with a single swipe. A handle at the proximal end of the shaft enables the user to apply force, pressing the attached cleaning elements against the windshield.

US-8826467.summary: The patent describes a glove designed to absorb and retain liquid, featuring a base layer for the user's hand, an absorbent storage layer, an attachment layer with mechanisms for removable attachment, and an application layer with corresponding mechanisms. The storage layer has a discontinuous surface with openings that allow fluid communication between the storage layer and the application layer. The glove may include a sleeve extending beyond the wrist with a fold to hold liquid, and the storage layer may be limited to the palm and finger area. The base layer can be made from synthetic rubber, such as nitrile.
key_claim_elements: A glove adapted to absorb and retain liquid, comprising a base layer for receiving a user's hand, a storage layer attached to the base layer that is absorbent and able to retain and subsequently dispense fluid, an attachment layer with mechanisms for removable attachment, and an application layer with corresponding mechanisms for removable attachment.
The storage layer has a discontinuous surface with row portions defining openings that enable fluid communication between the storage layer and the application layer.
The mechanisms on the inner side of the application layer and the exterior side of the attachment layer may comprise a hook-and-loop fastener.
The glove may include a sleeve extending beyond the wrist of a user, with a fold at the end of the sleeve to hold liquid.
The storage layer may be provided only around the palm and finger area of the glove.
The base layer may be made from up to 100% synthetic rubber, such as nitrile.

challenges: Designing a leak-resistant fluid path without powered pumps
Selecting porous dispenser material with repeatable flow
Retaining and repositioning a fabric wiper around a stiff core
Avoiding mold cavities and tolerance issues for wiper core fit
Keeping assembly simple for a small non-electronic manufacturer
US-10052665.rationale: The patent fits the intended manual household cleaning category because it combines a fluid dispenser with a wiping surface, and the disclosed features such as a porous fluid element, stiff-core fabric wiper, repositionable wiper, and simple housing cavities can be implemented without electronics. Its commercial relevance is moderate rather than high because the core idea is functionally straightforward and likely not unique enough to carry a product line by itself. Engineering effort is moderate because a small manufacturer would need to solve fluid storage, porous dispensing, wiper retention, and replacement or repositioning, but does not need complex electronics or precision manufacturing. The maintenance-fee lapse is a meaningful signal that the owner did not treat this as a high-value standalone asset, so it should not be viewed as a blocking risk or a premium differentiator. That signal may not fully apply to a new entrant because the patent is now expired and can be used freely, and a small maker could use the disclosed structure as one feature in a broader product, a refill system, or a niche customer need that the original owner did not prioritize.

US-10052751.rationale: Height adjustment is a standard feature in manual cleaning tools like mops. The described lock system offers a specific mechanical solution. Relevance is moderate as it applies to a subset of intended products. Engineering effort is moderate due to multiple components (cylinder, shoe, handle). Expired status removes IP barriers. Previous owner nonpayment suggests limited value to them, but new entrants can leverage the public domain technology for product differentiation without licensing costs.

US-10064481.rationale: The patent describes a specialized industrial component rather than a general household tool. The mechanical complexity is high for a simple manual product. The expired status offers freedom to operate but suggests limited original market value.

challenges: No market sizes, prices or sales figures
US-8800092.rationale: The patent describes a flat mop with a single trigger mechanism to remove disposable cloths without touch, which aligns directly with the intended product category of manual cleaning tools. The expiration due to non-payment places the technology in the public domain, eliminating licensing barriers. However, the mechanism involves molded steel pins and cover members, requiring specific tooling.

US-8826467.rationale: The patent describes a wearable cleaning device rather than the handled tools specified in the product intent. While it fits the broad non-powered category, it diverges from the core list of mops, brushes, and scrapers. Engineering is straightforward involving layered materials without electronics. The expiration due to non-payment suggests low historical commercial success, reducing infringement risk but indicating potential market fit issues. However, as public domain technology, it could serve as a low-cost accessory to bundle with core handled tools.

US-8826487.rationale: Direct category match for manual mop tools. Expired status eliminates licensing barriers. Mechanical complexity is moderate.

prose.executive_summary: The run looked at 2404 US utility patents in the cleaning-tool CPC groups. 299 of them appear in Official Gazette expiration notices from the last 104 weeks, 209 passed the non-powered screen and 8 were analysed. Recommended for technical and legal review: US 8,800,092 (Apparatus to remove a disposable cloth from a hand operated flat mop through a single trigger mechanism without having to touch the disposable cloth), US 8,826,487 (Mop cleaning set). Every status is dated and comes from public notices; none of this is legal clearance.
prose.methodology: Candidates came from the BigQuery PatentsView tables, filtered to core cleaning-tool CPC groups. Their patent numbers were matched against 104 weeks of Official Gazette expiration notices. Patents with a powered co-classification or a power source in an independent claim were removed. Every later reinstatement list was scanned before a patent was called expired, and confidence was set by rule from the number of sources and the completeness of that scan. 8 candidates were summarised and scored.
prose.commercial: US 8,800,092: commercial relevance 5/5, engineering effort 3/5. US 8,826,487: commercial relevance 5/5, engineering effort 3/5. US 10,052,665: commercial relevance 3/5, engineering effort 3/5. US 10,052,751: commercial relevance 3/5, engineering effort 3/5. US 10,065,611: commercial relevance 1/5, engineering effort 1/5. US consumer units spent an average of $844 on housekeeping supplies in 2025 (BLS); that is category context, not a market size for any candidate. An owner who stops paying maintenance fees usually judged the patent worth little to them, so each case needs a reason that judgement does not apply to a new entrant.
prose.next_steps: For US 8,800,092, check whether the trigger mechanism is manual or powered and verify the tooling for the molded steel pins and cover members before product work. For US 8,826,487, check the related active continuation and clarify whether the mop cleaning set is powered before product work.
